slot_note: Batch 3 re-root of the forecasting slot (numbered from seed FC09); architecture v1's irrigation-district world is closed and its identity sits in lineage. Architecture v2 is a new world, dataset and shell in the same client domain and task type: a river town's levee district deciding its 2027 levee raise against the 1 per cent annual chance flood.
niche: a town levee's design flood estimated at a downstream gauge whose large early floods were attenuated by a floodplain that upstream agricultural levee districts closed off with raises between 1994 and 2008
answer: Raise the Orrinsford levee crown by 2 ft before the 2027 flood season (design discharge 110,000 cfs at the Orrinsford gauge).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the district standard and every file correctly runs Bulletin 17C on the town gauge's 1962 to 2026 annual peaks, finds no trend or change point, reads each levee station's design water surface off the hydraulic rating and files that the levee holds the 1 per cent flood with its freeboard and needs no raise, when the record's large pre-raise floods were cut by a floodplain the river no longer has.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the 1 per cent annual chance discharge at the levee under the river as it now runs, which flood hydrology estimates by frequency analysis on a record representative of the present channel and floodplain, here the town's post-raise peaks extended through a longer unaffected upstream gauge; with a hospital or a school in its place there is no floodplain storage, no levee raise and no flood record to restore, so the task stops existing.
layer1: clocks mixed (UTC telemetry, local standard time legacy logger)
logger swap and a gauge datum change
stakeholder_role: the levee district's engineer, preparing the 2027 capital plan for the board

spine.entity: one hourly reading of gauge height and discharge at the upstream streamgauge
spine.source: constructed (the State Water Survey's hourly export)

world.org_type: a levee and drainage district protecting a river town

driver: A forward design value is fitted to a record whose large events were partly absorbed by a storage that has since been removed, so the record's upper tail understates the forward one; the present behaviour shows only in the few large events since the removal, and carrying a longer unaffected upstream record through that present relation restores a series the design value can be fitted to.
driver_concrete: The town gauge's large floods before the upstream levee districts raised their levees (1996 to 2008, the last in force from water year 2009) were attenuated by a floodplain those levees have since closed off, so the district standard's log-Pearson fit on the town's 1962 to 2026 peaks files no raise; the post-raise relation between the two gauges' peaks, carried onto the upstream gauge's unaffected record beside the town's own post-raise peaks, gives the present 1 per cent discharge and a 2 ft raise.
stump: A competent analyst fits the district standard's log-Pearson Type III curve to the town gauge's 1962 to 2026 annual peaks, finds no trend or change point and files that the levee holds the 1 per cent flood with its freeboard, no raise (95,000 cfs); the step that lands it there is taking the town's record as the present river's when its large pre-raise floods were cut by a floodplain the upstream levees have since closed off, which only the two gauges' peaks of the same floods, compared across the raises, show.

differentiation.task104: task104 re-thresholds a self-adapting scorer's log at a setting it never ran at; here no scorer or threshold is replayed: a flood record whose large events were attenuated by a floodplain since closed off is restored by carrying an unaffected upstream gauge's record through the two gauges' post-raise relation.
differentiation.task171: task171 v5 reads an exposure-response slope only where the response could not yet change how the input is lost; here no unit's response feeds back on its input: the downstream record's large floods were cut by floodplain storage that upstream levee raises removed, and the post-raise relation between the two gauges restores the series a frequency fit needs.
differentiation.task168: task168 completes the demand of units observed only until they reached a cap from units that never reached it; here nothing is capped or completed: the town's record is homogeneous only after the upstream levee raises, and the design flood rests on the upstream gauge's unaffected peaks carried through the post-raise relation.
differentiation.task138: The slot's architecture v1 rebuilt a soil store's start state for an irrigation order replay; architecture v2 shares no world, file or mechanism with it: a flood record made non-homogeneous in its upper tail by a floodplain the river no longer has is restored through a second gauge's record.

lineage.driver: A forward requirement replayed over past driver traces has to start every trace from the store each unit actually holds at the forecast date, rebuilt from each unit's own last recorded replenishment and the observed drawdown since; starting every trace full, letting each trace inherit the store its own past year left, or rebuilding the store from the model's replenishment rule instead of the record each understates it, because most units were last replenished weeks before the rule would have replenished them and the interval since was dry.
lineage.fate: superseded 2026-10-14 at round 2: the 10/10 audit (COMPLIANT_WEAK) found the start-state fork and the stump the same gap (no filed sentence fixed the 1 February state; the judge's DETERMINISTIC was conditional on it), the decisive step visible (the 64,887-row orders file the one large non-distractor file the default path never read, Table 1's November to January coefficients, the weather to 31 January 2027; the judge and the reader both found it unprompted) and Ask A's meter chaining crackable through the shop log's registers; never on the portal

lineage.driver: A forward requirement replayed over past driver traces starts every trace from the store each unit holds at the forecast date, and that store has to be rebuilt by running each unit's recorded replenishments through the season from the last time the record shows it full, because units run at a working deficit are replenished by about what they used and never return to full: taking each unit's last recorded replenishment as a refill, starting every trace full or spinning the model up on its own refill rule each leaves out the deficit the operation carried into the off-season.
lineage.fate: superseded 2026-10-15 at round 3: the rule 3 audit (VERDICT FAIL, rule application) found the start state the procedure's own daily balance (WOP 3.1 to 3.3) executed on the 2026 delivery record at Table 4's efficiency, which the table defined as the share of delivered water the root zone receives, so the filed sentences executed word for word gave the golden (215,000) with nothing left to estimate; that route is now round 3's default path; never on the portal

lineage.driver: A forward requirement replayed over past driver traces starts from each unit's store at the forecast date, rebuilt by running each unit's recorded inputs through the balance at the share of each input that reaches the store; the design share is not the record's, and only the monitored units' readings through the input season identify the record's share, because at the forecast date every monitored unit's store is the same under any share: carrying the design share, the monitored units' end-point readings, their offset or their share of capacity to the unmonitored units misstates the units replenished late in the season, on which the order turns.
